claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar microstructure.
The starting alloy has strength and plasticity below industrial fastener requirements.
The proposed intervention is to increase the alloy's carbon content.
Increasing carbon content will promote in situ formation of nanoscale carbides.
Carbon addition will produce finely dispersed carbides within the lamellar matrix.
The carbides will provide precipitation hardening.
The carbides will impede dislocation motion.
Carbon-induced carbide formation will improve grain-boundary cohesion.
The carbon-modified alloy will have greater yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The carbon-modified alloy will have greater plasticity or ductility than the baseline alloy.
The carbon-modified alloy will have greater resistance to room-temperature creep than the baseline alloy.
The carbon-modified alloy will have greater corrosion resistance than the baseline alloy.
The proposed improvement is applicable from extreme-cold to moderately elevated operating temperatures.
The proposed improvement is applicable during long-term loading at a significant fraction of yield strength.
The proposed improvement is applicable in saltwater and acidic corrosive environments.
A greater than 10% improvement in at least two measured properties is the proposed criterion for retaining the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts improvement in strength, plasticity, room-temperature creep resistance, and corrosion resistance, but the falsification rule requires improvement in only two measured properties. It could therefore retain the hypothesis even if one or more explicitly predicted properties are unchanged or degraded.
